prerequisites: Fundamentals of Mathematics and Computer Science

learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the importance of logic for intelligent problem-solving.

Logic is ubiquitous in understanding all aspects of daily experiences and interpersonal communication. A deepened understanding of these connections enables students to present comprehensible and logical arguments.

Artificial Intelligence programming systems use various types of logic with different expressive power. Students can create computer programs with logic suitable for solving specific application problems.

Logic connects fundamental theoretical concepts of epistemology with a ubiquitous use in human communication. Students deepen their abilities to deal with theoretical concepts and connect them with practical tasks.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the family of logic languages
Important basic building blocks and concepts of logic
Curry-Howard Isomorphism: propositions as types, proofs as programs
Programming in the language of logic
Rules, their syntax in the language of ASP and their correspondence in logic
Basic building blocks of programs: constants, variables, operators, literals, predicates, functional terms
The Clingo system for processing ASP programs
Concepts for compact representation of ASP programs: intervals and pooling
Arithmetic and its use in ASP programs
Exercises based on logic puzzles, classical Operations Research (OR) tasks and games (Sudoku)
Typical approaches to creating ASP programs
Aggregates in ASP: counting elements of a set, summation, maximum and minimum
assessment_rules: The examination is a 90-minute written exam.
